messages:
alex.s: FYI customer Cascade wants a Private/VPC deployment but keeps insisting they need source IP preservation for downstream webhooks. asking if PrivateLink is compatible with BYOIP egress and static IPs.
marie.se: Quick answer: PrivateLink (interface endpoint) -> our connector sits in their VPC so source IPs are preserved only if traffic originates inside their VPC or via routed peering. if they use our outbound proxy/egress NAT we typically SNAT.
josh.netops: Correct. Typical patterns:
- Peering/transit: preserves client srcIP end-to-end (but no AWS PrivateLink).
- PrivateLink: traffic enters via ENIs -> from our side it looks like connector IPs (we SNAT behind NLB).
So if they must see orig srcIP, peering or an L3 transit approach is required.
priya.infosec: Also callout: if they do TLS-inspect on the path and rewrite SNI, it can break cert pinning for webhook targets. need note in security questionnaire.
alex.s: They asked about firewall rules and single-port allowlists. Any minimal list we can give ops?
marie.se: Provide this stub to them:
```
- egress to 52.10.0.0/16 (Redwood connector pool) TCP 443
- inbound from customer VPC -> connector SG: 10.0.0.0/16 TCP 443 (if peering)
- allow outbound DNS 53/UDP to customer resolver (if using local DNS)
```
But emphasize PrivateLink uses interface ENIs so you also need to allow the interface endpoint IPs they create.
josh.netops: For PrivateLink + static egress IPs we can offer two options:
1) Customer accepts SNAT to our managed EIPs (we expose static EIPs per region) -> add NAT gateway outbound pricing (customer pays egress to internet + EIP costs).
2) Customer hosts an NLB in their VPC with target group to our connector (VPCE inside their account) and preserves client IPs but they must manage HA and scale.
marie.se: Option 1 is simplest for them; pricing note to include: per-EIP hourly + per-GB egress. i'll draft numbers.
priya.infosec: Also need to answer their security questionnaire item: 'Do you perform TLS termination in Redwood?' Answer: yes for hosted proxy flows; for Private deployment we can provide option to terminate in-customer VPC only if they host the NLB and run our connector privately.
alex.s: They also asked about who owns certs and rotation.
marie.se: We'll manage connector certs by default. If customer wants certs under their control, we can support customer-provided certs on their NLB. Document that in the SOW.
alex.s: Customer wants a runbook for failover if our managed EIP pool is unavailable.
josh.netops: Add this snippet to runbook:
```
- Detect connector outage -> traffic shifts to fallback region via routing policy (30s TTL)
- If using PrivateLink, re-register ENIs -> automatic via infra scripts
- For peering: BGP withdraw + route failover to alternate TGW (if configured)
```
marie.se: I'll ask infra to confirm whether we can reserve a dedicated EIP block for this customer for POC (affects pricing). @deploy-bot can you check current EIP availability in us-east-1?
deploy-bot: Checking EIP pool availability in us-east-1... 12 EIPs available, 4 currently reserved for customers.
priya.infosec: One more security Q: data path – is customer payload inspected/retained in Redwood logs? must state retention and encryption. we should attach our SOC2 section and the compliance snippet.
alex.s: ok i'll bundle: network rules, two architecture diagrams (peering vs privatelink), pricing delta for EIP + egress, and answers for TLS/cert ownership + runbook. target to send back to customer by EOD tomorrow.
marie.se: i'll draft diagrams and include this note: 'If webhook receivers require orig srcIP, choose peering or self-hosted NLB. PrivateLink provides simpler onboarding but will present connector IPs to your downstream systems.'
josh.netops: Also call out latency tradeoffs: peering avoids extra SNAT hop; PrivateLink can add ~2-6ms depending on AZ crossing. include perf table in doc.
alex.s: Great. tagging lineup: @marie.se to draft, @josh.netops for runbook + network snippet, @priya.infosec to review security questionnaire answers. I'll loop in the customer after draft. :thumbsup:
